standout_why: I compared against these pages. Apple 102423 (cited) covers protocol only: SMB, and no AFP from macOS 27. It names no NAS and no prices. The Synology KB page (cited) loaded with no article body when opened. Laptopbee (rank 12) names the DXP2800, DS223j, DH2300, DS223, DS225+ and others, but every model has only a 'Check Price on Amazon' link: no prices, no wattage, no dB figures and no update-support dates. It never mentions Ubiquiti. Synology's compare pages (ranks 4–9) give noise and power for DS223, DS223j and DS225+ but no prices and no non-Synology models. The B&H compare pages (ranks 19–23) list DH2300, DXP2800, F2-425 and QNAP models, but they return 403, so I can't confirm what prices they showed. None of the results ChatGPT got includes Ubiquiti. That gives two new facts: the $199 UNAS 2 and UGREEN's dated store price below the DS223.
decides: This challenges ChatGPT's value pick. Its 'best value' DS223 ($304.99, 1GbE, 2 GB) costs more than two 2.5GbE boxes from the makers' own stores: UniFi UNAS 2 at $199.00 and UGREEN DH2300 at $239.99. That supports a cheaper 2.5GbE pick, as long as the page also proves Time Machine works on it. Synology's own spec table confirms the DS223 is the quietest of its three at 14.6 dB(A), against 18.2 for the DS223j and 19.6 for the DS225+. So the DS223 keeps a quiet-room argument, not a price or speed one. The DXP2800 ($389.99) and F2-425 Plus ($469.99) cost more than the DS225+ card, and the extra money buys nothing for backup-only use.
